profile.address: Via Caldera, Settimo Milanese, Milan, Italy
profile.reading: This is Avalon 2, a data center on Via Caldera in the Settimo Milanese area on Milans western edge, less than 3 kilometers from the original Avalon 1 building, built and inaugurated in 2020 by Irideos as the first expansion of the Avalon Campus. The facility offers about 650 kilowatts of IT power across about 300 square meters, or roughly 3,200 square feet, of floor space, with ground floor load capacity rated to 1,500 kilograms per square meter, powered on a claimed 100 percent renewable electricity supply, and connected to Avalon 1 by two separate fiber paths using 192 cables, expandable to 720, supporting speeds up to 400 gigabits per second, with a distributed meet me room linking all Avalon campus buildings and 24 hour network operations center monitoring. Irideos itself was founded in August 2018 through infrastructure fund manager F2i, together with the Marguerite fund, consolidating four Italian telecom companies, Infracom, MC-link, KPNQwest Italia, and Enter, with MC-link serving as the entity rebranded as Irideos; the company absorbed Clouditalia Telecomunicazioni in November 2020, and Asterion Industrial Partners acquired a majority stake in 2022, reaching about 98 percent ownership by the deals completion that December. On August 1, 2024, Irideos was merged by incorporation into Retelit Digital Services, alongside a separate merger of Brennercom, ending Irideos as an independently operating company; both firms were already commonly owned by Asterion Industrial Partners before the legal merger. As a result, this Avalon 2 building and Retelits own Avalon 3 building are now both owned and operated by Retelit as parts of one unified Avalon Campus alongside Avalon 1, which the merged company markets as the most interconnected data center campus in Italy. Retelit and its predecessor Irideos both grew substantially under Asterion Industrial Partners ownership through a mix of organic build-out and acquisition, a pattern reflected in the way this Avalon 2 building itself passed from an independent Irideos to Retelit control without a change in physical operations.
